Messages.Author: Noal McDonald
Messages.Body:
"GreySeer" <e...@i.think.not> wrote:
> Biggest problem is that you have to pay 2+capacity to contest the vampire.

Dreams, Montreal, Tomb and Enchant Kindred could bring the cost down.
Zillah's Valley could help speed up the process at a small cost. I
would also add some Stranger Among Us cards to get the Trujah and any
scarce vampires others are playing. Betrayer could be used to help
cause pool damage until you get them out.

Obviously, there's some fat listed that would have to be trimmed down.

> If you did do it, you'd only put into your crypt vampires that you see often
> and you want for youeself or really annoy you. Like Arika if you're playing

> vote deck, or Beast if you're playing a rush/S:CE deck.

You're missing the point entirely. The deck that exploits this would
be all about bring out vampires, contesting them with others and then
burning their copy. You've paid for the vampire and get to keep it.
They've paid for the vampire and don't. This wouldn't be a vote deck
or a rush deck. This is a resource theft deck.

Decks that use mid to large capacity vampires would be utterly screwed
by this. Weenie hordes would largely be unaffected, I would think,
unless you added some Domain Challenge votes. You'd have to a lot of
bleed defense and a light amount of vote and combat defense.

This would take a fair amount of R&D to get the proportions right, but
it could be pretty vicious if done right.

Regards,
Noal

Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin
Messages.Body:
"Noal McDonald" <dhar...@my-deja.com> wrote in message

news:bb705c59.02052...@posting.google.com...

> Oh god...Agaitas with a vampire stealing deck would be just plain
> rude. You steal your prey's vampires and play his deck against him.
> Has anyone done this yet?

Yeah.

So far it's pretty weak. I've tried Agaitas/Salubri/Spirit
Marionette, which works OK except that it's only actually
good if your prey is playing a bleed deck (stealth-bleed even
better). Agaitas/Hostile Takeover has the problem that you're
paying your prey pool for the vamps you steal, if you can even
afford them. (It usually turns out that you're (I'm) not
willing to pay what it would take rather than just let my prey
bleed himself for, say, 4 to keep the vamp.) Agaitas/ToGP
might be slightly better except that (a) you have to have out
at least 15 capacity of vampires to do this (unless getting
Justicars with vote cards, somewhat excessively tricky), (b)
it costs 3 up front, and (c) using Agaitas is probably not
the key to winning with this deck.

I've also tried Agaitas/Ian Forestal and that hasn't done very
well either.

Agaitas, so far, seems to be pretty cute but not very effective
(at least for me) in actually letting you play your prey's
deck (unless by some chance your prey is using exactly the
right cards for you to be able to play them).

My guess is that this is largely because you'll never be able
to play your prey's deck as well as he can. You only ever
get a 3-4 card "hand" of his deck (unless you manage to play
*everything* from your hand and replace with his, unlikely
and not necessarily even desirable) and don't have as many
vampires with the right skills as he does.

Josh

theorizin'

<snip your deck which I have copied with a few changes>

It is sort of a silly concept, but it could be quite fun, and powerful
as long as your predator or prey wasn't playing a real rush deck.

My version of the crypt would be every vampire in the game plus
Synesios 4 times. No one is actually going to get 150 Synesios, and
anyway you would need more like 225 or something. The Library just has
an extra recruitment. I decided that one Stranger Among us wasn't
worth it because you couldn't count on drawing it first, and if you
drew it later it wouldn't help unless your target was playing scarce
vamps.

If someone does get a hundred Synesios, then they should take out all
the vamps that no one plays with and every vampire 3 and below, as
they aren't worth stealing. If this deck will work, it will operate
on the same principle as an all bloat deck. Get out loads of minions
that you barely pay for and swarm.

Anyway here is my version of the Library:

Library: (90 cards)
-------------------
Master (40 cards)
5 Betrayer
3 Golconda: Inner Peace
4 Information Highway
11 Minion Tap
6 Parthenon, The
11 Recruitment

Action (10 cards)
10 Clio's Kiss

Action Modifier (18 cards)
1 Cloak the Gathering
10 Domain of Evernight
1 Faceless Night
4 Forgotten Labyrinth
1 Lost in Crowds
1 Spying Mission

Reaction (8 cards)
5 Deflection
3 Delaying Tactics

Combat (14 cards)
4 Dodge
7 Fake Out
3 Majesty

Despite what someone said about the Parthenon being unique, you really
really need it. I should even put a rumors in, but eh.... The combat
defense module should work against stupid Immortal Grapple and casual
combat. The dodges will actually work on the minions you get that
*don't* have presence. Betrayer rocks, but remember that you need to
recruit at least 2 of your prey's vamps in order to make them take
more than 2 per betrayer.

I think your version was really short on the blood gain. After paying
for 2 recruitments and Synesios, if you don't draw a minion tap (4/90
ain't good odds) then you are dead against any competitive deck.

Comments?

Colin Riggs

I'll play 3-4 corruptions a turn and get a embrace or 2 back in my hand and
bring out another Vamp, prob a big one with OBF,SER,PRE and find the Kobar
Towers along the way. After 8-9 turns I'll have 7-9 minions of my own and
at least 1 5+ cap from someone else. I have a few Con Boon in the deck just
in case I can make friends with some cross table votes and I find a rave is
handy now and then. Unless heavy bleed is my preditor then I don't really
run into pool shortages too quickly. I love to sit as the preditor of low
cap PRE bleed or, (even better) low cap PRE vote! Not a deck that will
sweep every table it sits down at but one that is fun to play and is good at
what it does.
